::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 16 [1895]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Bodleian Library, Oxford: English Letters: e.174 ff 159-61
:::

Dear [Mr Bullock](people/person_221.qmd),
I will try to do [Raymond Lull](cmy_books/cmybook_358.qmd) in short by the end of next week, I have both the books.[^1]

You will be glad to hear that I have had a cheerful letter from Miss [Florence Wilford](people/person_1520.qmd) well, and at home with her [sister](people/person_1519.qmd)[^2]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Envelope addressed to ‘The Revd  J.F.  Bullock/Radwinter Rectory/Saffron Walden.’ Postmark MR 16/95.
[^2]: Raymond Lull (1232-1315), missionary and philosopher.
[^3]: Florence Wilford seems to have been confined in a lunatic asylum in later life.
